info.title: Thaniumnine Data API
info.description:
> **Building data. Connected.**
>
> Integrate your applications with the Thaniumnine Data API. Explore building measurements, asset information and engineering workflows through a single REST API.
>
> [Get started](#description/getting-started) · [FDD scheduling guide](#tag/fdd-findings)

## Explore the API

- **[Authentication](#tag/authentication)**
  Obtain and refresh access tokens.
- **[Aggregation records](#tag/aggregation-records)**
  Read and ingest aggregated measurements.
- **[Device history](#tag/device-history)**
  Discover devices and retrieve historical point data.
- **[Device metadata](#tag/device-metadata)**
  Access device definitions and asset information.
- **[FDD findings](#tag/fdd-findings)**
  Explore fault detection and the finding-to-schedule workflow.
- **[Schedule entries](#tag/schedule-entries)**
  Create, update and retrieve engineering schedules.

## Getting started

**Base URL** (local development)

```text
http://localhost:3500/api/v1
```

1. Obtain an access token using `POST /auth/login`.
2. Include `Authorization: Bearer <access_token>` on protected requests.
3. Choose an API category above or use the sidebar to explore endpoints.

Use `POST /auth/refresh` to refresh your session and `POST /auth/logout` to revoke it. All endpoint paths are relative to `/api/v1`.

## About this reference

Examples use illustrative identifiers and response payloads. Live requests are disabled by default. Use an authorised disposable test database for local write operations, and never use production credentials or customer data in examples.

## Developer guide: From finding to scheduled task

This walkthrough shows how an FDD finding becomes a scheduled engineering task. Each step uses an identifier returned by the preceding step.

**FDD finding → Assignment → Task → Schedule entry**

All requests use `example-org` as the organisation. Replace it and the sample identifiers with values from your authorised test environment. JSON requests use `Content-Type: application/json`. Include your bearer access token on each request. The response excerpts below are illustrative and show selected fields only.

### Step 1 — Retrieve FDD findings

```http
GET /organisations/example-org/fdd
```

Select a finding from the returned `records` array. For this example, use `fdd_history_id` **6**.

```json
{
  "records": [
    {
      "fdd_history_id": "6",
      "rule_id": "FDD_FCU_CONTROL_LOOP_HUNTING_OR_UNST_008",
      "closed": false,
      "building": "example-building",
      "device_id": "FCU-000001",
      "room": "Office 201"
    }
  ],
  "count": 1
}
```

### Step 2 — Assign the finding

```http
POST /organisations/example-org/fdd/6/assignments
```

Request body:

```json
{
  "firebase_user_id": "example-user-id"
}
```

Example response excerpt:

```json
{
  "id": "51",
  "fdd_history_id": "6",
  "firebase_user_id": "example-user-id"
}
```

Save the returned `id` (**51**). This is the assignment ID, not the FDD history ID.

### Step 3 — Create a task

```http
POST /organisations/example-org/tasks
```

Pass the assignment ID in the `assignment_ids` array.

```json
{
  "assignment_ids": ["51"]
}
```

Example response:

```json
{
  "task_id": "15",
  "assignment_ids": ["51"]
}
```

Save the returned `task_id` (**15**) for the next request. A task can group assignment records; the array contains assignment IDs, not finding IDs.

### Step 4 — Schedule the task

```http
POST /organisations/example-org/tasks/15/schedule-entries
```

Request body:

```json
{
  "scheduled_time": "2026-11-27T09:00:00.000Z",
  "status": "Planned",
  "is_locked": false
}
```

Example response excerpt:

```json
{
  "id": "00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000005",
  "task_id": "15",
  "scheduled_time": "2026-11-27T09:00:00.000Z",
  "status": "Planned",
  "is_locked": false
}
```

The returned `id` is the schedule entry UUID. Keep it alongside `task_id` if you need to update the booking later. The timestamp uses UTC (`Z`).

### Step 5 — Retrieve the organisation schedule

```http
GET /organisations/example-org/schedule-entries?from=2026-11-26&to=2026-11-30
```

Find the newly created entry in `records` by its schedule entry UUID. The organisation schedule includes assignment details for each scheduled task, allowing a calendar to display the associated engineer and finding.

### How the identifiers connect

| Identifier | Example | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `fdd_history_id` | `6` | Identifies the finding. |
| Assignment `id` | `51` | Identifies the assignment record; used in `assignment_ids`. |
| `task_id` | `15` | Identifies the task that groups assignments. |
| Schedule entry `id` | `00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000005` | Identifies the calendar booking. |

To reschedule this booking, use `PATCH /organisations/example-org/tasks/15/schedule-entries/00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000005` with a new `scheduled_time`.
